title: Differences across six scoring areas
reading_key: Dots show averages; lines contain the middle 95% from 20,000 repeated draws of the stated records. Zero means no average difference. These ranges describe sensitivity to the saved observations, not all sources of judging error or a representative population. Right of zero favors the skeptical side. These are area scores before weighting, not additive contributions.

title: The difference is smaller in the additions
scope: Counts shown per row; overlapping selections
reading_key: Dots show averages; lines contain the middle 95% from 20,000 repeated draws of the stated records. Zero means no average difference. These ranges describe sensitivity to the saved observations, not all sources of judging error or a representative population. Parentheses count comparisons. Rows overlap and are not independent replications.

title: Where the overall score difference comes from
reading_key: Bar lengths show additive weighted contributions, not independent causes. The small rounding residual and any burden adjustment reconcile their sum with the overall gap; both are reported in the text.

title: Topic gaps: ordering remains uncertain
reading_key: Dots show averages; lines contain the middle 95% from 20,000 repeated draws of the stated records. Zero means no average difference. These ranges describe sensitivity to the saved observations, not all sources of judging error or a representative population. Counts are in parentheses. These stable research groups are not the current browsing categories.

title: Support gap by kind of assessed move
scope: Both sides must contain the stated move kind; equal debate weights
reading_key: Dots show averages; lines contain the middle 95% from 20,000 repeated draws of the stated records. Zero means no average difference. These ranges describe sensitivity to the saved observations, not all sources of judging error or a representative population. Each side’s qualifying moves are averaged before comparing sides. Rows overlap; these are not official weighted overall scores.

title: How often does each topic have the largest gap?
reading_key: Each bar counts calculations in which the topic has the highest gap. This is a stability exercise, not the probability that it is truly the hardest topic in the wider world.

title: Historical direct review: September 5, 2026
scope: 187 previously reviewed transcripts, not the expanded archive
reading_key: Rust is theist; teal is non-theist. Each debate receives equal weight after allowing for speech length. Both panels start at zero on the same scale. Protected slogans are a subset of unsupported slogans; do not add them. These dated counts have not been extended to new transcripts.

title: The narrower historical finding is clearer
unit: Theist minus non-theist uses per 10,000 words
reading_key: Dots show averages; lines contain the middle 95% from 20,000 repeated draws of the stated records. Zero means no average difference. These ranges describe sensitivity to the saved observations, not all sources of judging error or a representative population. The unsupported-slogan range crosses zero; the protected-slogan range does not. Both use the September direct annotations, not new scorecard judgments.

title: Current scores: a separate warning pattern
unit: Religious minus skeptical flagged share (percentage points)
scope: Support <70, clarity <80 and care <80 together; not direct slogan detection
reading_key: Dots show averages; lines contain the middle 95% from 20,000 repeated draws of the stated records. Zero means no average difference. These ranges describe sensitivity to the saved observations, not all sources of judging error or a representative population. A flag requires all three score thresholds on the same move. A low score does not demonstrate a criticism-blocking slogan. Never combine these percentages with the transcript word rates.

title: Role estimates answer different questions
scope: Debate draws for first two rows; speaker draws for last two
reading_key: Dots show averages; lines contain the middle 95% from 20,000 repeated draws of the stated records. Zero means no average difference. These ranges describe sensitivity to the saved observations, not all sources of judging error or a representative population. Right of zero favors CON. The weighted same-speaker range is now above zero, but no comparison randomly assigns roles, opponents or topics.

title: The positions matter to the role contrast
reading_key: Dots show averages; lines contain the middle 95% from 20,000 repeated draws of the stated records. Zero means no average difference. These ranges describe sensitivity to the saved observations, not all sources of judging error or a representative population.

title: Lower-scoring sides with no named-fallacy tag
reading_key: Fractions count lower-scoring sides without a fallacy label over all decisive results in each group. The dark total includes the other groups. No tag does not mean no error. Counts are assessments, including the disclosed shared-video pair.

title: Untagged losses can be weaker across many areas
reading_key: Each bar counts losses with no named-fallacy label that trail in exactly the stated number of weighted scoring areas. Bars add to the eligible total; these are not independent deficiencies.

title: What the accepted labels actually record
reading_key: A move may carry several labels, so label instances exceed tagged moves. The six names are the accepted inventory in this snapshot, not an exhaustive catalogue of reasoning errors.

title: Returning speakers across assessment processes
scope: One dot per person appearing in both groups
reading_key: The horizontal coordinate is the earlier average and the vertical coordinate the later average. Below the diagonal means lower later. Both axes enlarge the observed score range. These are different performances, not the same debate judged twice.

title: Average debate score by assessment process
unit: Average of the two sides (score points)
scope: One equally weighted midpoint per comparable debate
reading_key: Dots show averages; lines contain the middle 95% from 20,000 repeated draws of the stated records. Zero means no average difference. These ranges describe sensitivity to the saved observations, not all sources of judging error or a representative population.

title: Any fallacy or bias tag, by assessment process
scope: Pooled move counts, not equal debate rates
reading_key: A move counts once if it has any fallacy or bias tag. Bar length is the percentage of all moves in that process. Different annotation rates can reflect procedure as well as different arguments.

title: The same scale can use different score vocabularies
unit: Share of moves at each exact mark
scope: All comparable moves, grouped by process
reading_key: Teal is earlier; rust is later. Each bar shows the share of moves assigned that exact area score. Both panels use identical axes. More distinct marks mean finer numerical resolution, not necessarily better judgments.

title: Leading averages have overlapping rank ranges
scope: Highest 15 means shown; all 57 eligible people included in calculation
reading_key: Dark dots are displayed places. Teal lines contain the middle 95% of ranks obtained by drawing again from recorded scores. Dashed rust lines use a model allowing variation estimated across the group. Parentheses count appearances. Neither line is a future-win probability.

title: Most people still have limited evidence
reading_key: Gray bars are below the three-appearance research threshold; teal bars enter the fixed field. A small sample is not a poor score.

title: More evidence helps; crowded averages still overlap
reading_key: Each dot is a person. Height is the upper rank endpoint minus the lower: 2–9 has width 7. Lower means a narrower calculated range, not a lower performance score. Rank density and score variation matter as well as sample size.
